text:
Cole Hutson is 20, was a second-round pick in 2024, and is playing 19 minutes a night for Washington with 11 points in 16 games. Five of them are goals, including a two-goal night in Nashville. Among defensemen drafted in that range since 2005, the median first full season is about 0.21 points a game. Hutson is at more than three times that.

The comparisons our numbers draw are telling: John Carlson, Rasmus Dahlin, Cale Makar. Not as equals, but as a style. He shoots a lot, sets teammates up, and the Capitals create a lot with him on the ice (55% of shot attempts at 5v5).

Some of it will cool. He is shooting 15.6% against a typical defenseman's 6.5%, and the team has scored nearly five more goals than its chances deserve with him out there. His goals are fueling an outsized wins-added number (49th of 515 skaters).

RMNB has written about how the Capitals are managing his ice time alongside Jack St. Ivany. The minutes are climbing. That is the trend we'd watch.
headline: Cole Hutson is already playing like a top-pair defenseman
